backend_impl: MEMORY CLAIM: "Triton also uses LESS memory (recomputes states instead of retaining the autograd graph)"
caveat: SUBSTANTIATED AT THE MEASURED SHAPES: Triton peak < torch peak in all 6 rows (e.g. 2.09 vs 5.65 GiB at B2/T8192/R4; 1.05 vs 2.83 at B4/T2048/R4). MECHANISM IS AS DESCRIBED: torch retains O(B*T*R*H*K*V) intermediate states; Triton's hs is O(B*T*H*K*V), i.e. R-times smaller, though it adds NV=8 partial buffers the torch path does not have. CAVEAT: this advantage INVERTS at large K,V -- the hs workspace is the documented OOM cliff (see limitations.tsv E1), so "uses less memory" is true at the probe shapes and false as a general statement.
